'''Courier missions''', also described as '''data delivery''' missions, require a commander to carry mission data from an issuing contact to a named destination. The data does not occupy cargo space, so even a ship without a Cargo Rack can normally complete the basic objective.

== Obtaining a courier mission ==

Courier contracts are offered by minor factions on the Mission Board. Availability depends on the station, faction, commander reputation, faction state, and the current mission selection.

Before accepting, record:

* the issuing faction;
* the origin system;
* the destination system and station or settlement;
* any named destination or target faction;
* the deadline and threat level;
* whether hostile ships may be sent;
* the available reward packages.

The journal's <code>MissionAccepted</code> event can include <code>Faction</code>, <code>TargetFaction</code>, <code>DestinationSystem</code>, <code>DestinationStation</code>, <code>Expiry</code>, and the displayed reputation or influence strength.<ref name="journalv38">[https://hosting.zaonce.net/community/journal/v38/Journal_Manual_v38.pdf Elite Dangerous Player Journal Manual, version 38], Frontier Developments, pp. 67–70.</ref>

== Completing the mission ==

# Plot a route to the destination system.
# Monitor the Transactions panel for mission updates and hostile warnings.
# Evade or defeat any mission-generated interdictions.
# Dock or land at the named destination.
# Open the Mission Board and select the highlighted completion contact.
# Choose a reward package and confirm completion.

No physical data item appears in the cargo hold. Ship choice can therefore prioritise jump range, speed, thermal control, shields, and access to the destination's pad size.

== Interdictions and hostile responses ==

A courier mission can generate hostile ships even though combat is not the objective. An update normally identifies the hostile commander or warns that enemies have been sent.

Practical options are:

* submit to the interdiction, boost away, and re-enter supercruise;
* win the interdiction minigame;
* destroy the attacker if the ship and legal situation make that sensible;
* use a fast or cool-running ship to reduce exposure.

Do not assume that destroying an attacker is required. Check the mission update: a combat bonus can be optional while the data delivery remains the actual completion condition.

== Failure and abandonment ==

Courier missions normally fail when the deadline expires or when a mission-specific failure condition is met. The data does not occupy a destructible cargo canister, but ship destruction can still cost time, rebuy, exploration data, vouchers, and other carried assets.

Abandoning the mission can reduce reputation and may have a negative mission effect. Frontier's journal records <code>MissionAbandoned</code> and <code>MissionFailed</code>, but those events do not include the detailed <code>FactionEffects</code> array used by <code>MissionCompleted</code>.<ref name="journalv38" />

== Rewards ==

Courier missions can offer credits, reputation, influence, materials, or commodities in different combinations. See [[Mission Rewards]].

For BGS work, do not assume that the influence icon belongs only to the issuer. Frontier's documented courier example records reputation for the issuing faction and an influence effect for a different target faction in the destination system.<ref name="journalv38" /> Use [[Courier Missions for BGS]] before taking a multi-faction courier contract for a campaign.

== Stacking ==

Several courier missions can be taken along the same route. This is '''route stacking''': each contract still has its own destination, deadline, completion contact, and reward. Delivering one data package does not normally complete unrelated courier contracts unless their own objectives are also satisfied.

Group offers by destination, then check supercruise distance and pad access. A route with many system jumps but short station approaches may be faster than a nominally nearby destination hundreds of thousands of light-seconds from arrival.

== Common mistakes ==

* Treating the issuer as proof of the influence recipient.
* Checking the system but not the exact destination station or settlement.
* Ignoring a distant secondary star or long supercruise leg.
* Accepting more deadlines than the route can support.
* Fighting every hostile ship when escape would protect the mission.
* Selecting an INF reward without checking the affected faction and system.
